The strongest refutation is the incalculability objection: the calculus asks us to total the pleasures and pains of every consequence of an act, including far-reaching and unforeseeable ones. Those consequences can't be known, and pleasures and pains have no common cardinal scale for summing across people, so the "sum" can't be computed even in principle. You didn't include the actual propositions, so I'm choosing on that basis. If one of them states this epistemic and measurement problem, that's the one I'd pick.

CONFIDENCE: 45
